title: Focus lattice: Q3 initiatives brief
body:
Purpose and framing:
- Short: synthesize a compact set of company-level commitments for Q3 that balance performance (latency/cost), reliability, and private-deploy momentum. This is an early draft intended for leadership alignment and the all-staff sync in Week 1 of the quarter.
- Outcome: an ordered set of 3 company OKR themes + candidate sub-initiatives, owners, and lightweight signals we can track in ProductOps dashboards.

Context notes (quick):
- Hosted API growth remains strong; ticket is to protect latency SLO while pushing price/perf improvements.
- Dedicated contracts pipeline expects two mid-market commitments that require SLA documentation and capacity knobs.
- Private pilot with a regulated customer is on a 10-week runway; privacy + KMS integration are blockers.

High-level themes (candidate company OKRs):
1) Operational predictability: keep 95th p99 latency degradation <10% during high-throughput windows and reduce per-token cost by 12% vs baseline.
   - Why: sales asks and PLG retention both hinge on predictable performance/costs.
   - Lead: Leo Zhang (eng-serve/infra).
   - Signals: p95/p99 latency dashboards; per-token $ cost by model bucket; number of incidents with customer-visible latency >SLA.

2) Enterprise readiness and expansion: close two Dedicated deals, complete enterprise SLA kit, and have private pilot reach production criteria.
   - Why: revenue de-risking and runway to scale Private product.
   - Lead: Maya Gonzalez (sales & solutions eng).
   - Signals: committed ARR from Dedicated, completed SLA docs, pilot readiness checklist pass.

3) Developer-first velocity: ship 2 SDK quality improvements + a reduced onboarding time for new customers (trial -> first production route in <14 days).
   - Why: PLG funnel improvement and lower onboarding support cost.
   - Lead: Jon Rivers (devx).
   - Signals: median time-to-first-call in trial, number of self-serve projects that reach 1k calls/week without SE help.

Candidate sub-initiatives (mapped to themes):
- Continuous batching pilot (theme 1): tune default batch sizing heuristics and KV cache TTLs; hypothesize 8–10% cost improvement for chat workloads. Milestone: runtime changes merged + canary pipeline by week 6. Owner: eng-serving-runtime. JIRA: JIRA-PROD-1182.
- SLA kit and legal checklist (theme 2): final legal language, incident definitions, scheduled maintenance policy, support SLAs. Deliverable: SLA playbook + template contract addendum. Owner: legal + product. Linked artifact: CONFLUENCE-PLAN-7421.
- Private deployment onboarding flow (theme 2 & 3): a simplified checklist (networking, KMS, audit logs) + a preflight validator script. Milestone: validator alpha for pilot by week 4. Owner: private-deployments team.
- SDK onboarding improvements (theme 3): quickstart recipe, a single-file example app, and improved sample prompts for quality testing. Owner: developer-experience.
- Eval/quality guardrails (cross-theme): maintain a weekly prompt set check for regressions against the top 10 customer prompts. Owner: Applied ML.

All-staff sync structure (Week 1 of Q3) — proposed run-of-show:
- 00:00–00:03 Opening: founders (0–3 min) — one-sentence focus + one ask to teams.
- 00:03–00:10 Metrics snapshot: product ops (top-line usage, latency p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens) — quick callouts.
- 00:10–00:25 Theme deep dives (3x 5 min): Operational predictability, Enterprise readiness, Developer velocity — each lead gives 3 key milestones.
- 00:25–00:30 Action slot: how to raise risks and where to file blockers (explicit triage path and owner list).
- Post-sync: breakouts by function for 30 min to register team-level OKRs and owners.

Communication plan and cadence:
- Pre-read to staff: this doc + 1-pager highlighting the three themes, distributed 72 hours before sync. Owner: product-ops.
- Weekly leadership checkpoint: 30 minutes Thurs; owners report status, blockers, and a single ask. Owner: Anika.
- Biweekly cross-team triage: working-level engineering/product ops to handle emergent capacity issues.

Risks / unknowns (triage list):
- Model performance regression after runtime change — need a rollback + quality eval plan. (Mitigation: staged canary + automatic rollback trigger.)
- Dedicated capacity scheduling conflicts with public cloud spot availability — require early capacity reservations or negotiated burst windows.
- Pilot compliance checklist slipping because customer legal reviews take longer. (Mitigation: early legal engagement + template contracts).

Immediate asks / decisions needed from execs (for alignment):
- Decision A: Confirm the top-line cost improvement target (12% vs baseline) is acceptable as a company-level KR.
- Decision B: Approve prioritization of private pilot KMS work above medium-priority infra tickets for the next 6 weeks.
- Decision C: Authorize 2 headcount-limited contractor seats for SDK/quickstart work to hit the 14-day onboarding target.

Notes-to-self / working reminders (rough):
- Collect top-10 customer prompt set from CS by Fri. Action: Priya to coordinate.
- Make a one-slide exec summary for Friday's leadership review.
- Ensure dashboards show both relative and absolute per-token cost so comms to sales are clear.

Open questions to resolve in first leadership checkpoint:
- How aggressive should the automated batching defaults be — conservative (small wins but safe) vs aggressive (higher savings but higher regression risk)?
- Do we require legal sign-off before public-facing SLA wording, or can we publish a ‘beta SLA’ to support sales?

Appendix: quick milestones timeline (weeks) — (for triage):
- Week 1: publish pre-read; sync and team breakouts; collect prompt sets.
- Week 2–4: implement validator + SDK quickstarts; start continuous batching canary.
- Week 5–8: Dedicated SLA kit complete; private pilot validator pass; deal negotiations advance.
- Week 9–12: rollouts, A/B checks, and exec check for Q3 mid-point.

Contact / ownership shorthand:
- ProductOps: Anika Patel (owner, overall rhythm)
- Eng Serving Runtime: Leo Zhang (latency/cost workstreams)
- Developer Experience: Jon Rivers (onboarding/SDK)
- Sales & Solutions: Maya Gonzalez (dedicated deals & pilots)
- Applied ML: Priya Nambiar (evals & quality)

Bottom-line: this is intentionally prioritized and lean — three company-level themes with clear owners and a tight 12-week rhythm. The immediate ask of execs is three alignment decisions (cost target, KMS prioritization, contractor OK).

TODO (near-term): finalize pre-read, get exec decisions by next Thurs, and publish the 1-pager to staff 72 hours before the sync.
